discovered-from:LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V

The slot_schedule removal (LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V) removes the time-based slot schedule from proxy/config.yaml, config-fast.yaml, config-cheap.yaml.

The proxy-usage-analysis skill (.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/) still parses slot_schedule from the active config to derive per-time slot counts and ctx: scripts/config_loader.py (_normalize), scripts/bucketing.py (schedule_from_config), scripts/reporting.py (ctx_by_time), scripts/recommendations.py (advice pointing at 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule').

Impact: with no slot_schedule key, config_loader omits it and bucketing falls back to a single 'fast' bucket with default_slots (session_slot_pool_size) for the whole day — the cheap (2-slot) vs fast (3-slot) slot-count split is lost.

Required work (in the skill directory, per .pi boundary this item must be explicitly authorized):
- Derive per-mode slot counts from the mode profiles' static session_slot_pool_size (fast 3 / cheap 2) instead of schedule entries.
- Replace ctx_by_time semantics with the profiles' static local_model_ctx_size.
- Update recommendations text that references 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule'.
- Update skill tests/fixtures accordingly.
data.title: proxy-usage-analysis: drop slot_schedule dependency after per-mode slot-count simplification

# Run the controlled N=3 (and N=4) slot-count sweep in a quiet/maintenance window

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the measured N=3/N=4 sweep that
`LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` could not complete on shared production, so the
concurrency-vs-capacity projection (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes;
N=3 ~6.7%) is validated or refuted against real local TTFT, decode speed,
queue-timeout rate and VRAM.

## Why this exists

The deterministic analysis in `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`
(AC1/AC2/AC4) is complete and recommends **keep N=2** pending this sweep. The
AC3 measured sweep was attempted on 2026-10-20 against the live proxy while it
was serving 5 concurrent sessions (52 distinct sessions / 5 min, 2 audits + 4
herdr panes holding local leases). Every benchmark turn-1 request stalled at
600–760 s (1200 s timeout) and llama-server stopped answering health probes, so
the run was aborted, the harness restored the config (sha256 `6eec5656…`) and a
controlled `start-proxy.sh --restart` returned the proxy to healthy (N=2,
`--parallel 2`).

## Task

Run the sweep in a window with no other local-lease holders (drain or stop
herdr panes / audits), using the same harness as the prior verdict
(`LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7` / `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`):

```
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
# then, if memory permits:
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --slots 4 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
```

Record per N: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, llama-server
startup + `--parallel` agreement (must match `session_slot_pool_size`), per-slot
KV memory and system MemAvailable. Then update the decision in
`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (or a successor doc) and,
if the verdict moves to N=3/N=4, create the config-change item that also
re-decides the warm-threshold = 95%-of-per-slot target (which becomes 79,121 at
N=3 vs 120,627 at N=2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A sweep run at N=2, N=3 (and N=4 if memory allows) with the harness above,
   with the results committed under `proxy/benchmarks/results/`.
2. The run records `--parallel` agreement, per-slot context clamp, and system
   MemAvailable, and explicitly notes any validity caveat (live leases, remote
   fallback) as the prior verdict did.
3. A recorded verdict (keep N=2 / move to N=3 / N=4) that reconciles the
   measured queue-timeout and denial rates with the concurrency projection in
   the reevaluation doc.

## Risks / notes

- N=3 clamps per-slot context to 83,285 (warm threshold 79,121); N=4 to 61,440.
- Prefill is serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), so more slots add
  decode concurrency, not prefill capacity.
- Do **not** run this against the shared proxy during active multi-agent work.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD** – Slot-count benchmark: find optimal session_slot_pool_size for Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MSC95VTC008GVR7** – Validate benchmark harness at 120K tokens (completed)
- **LP-0MVAZPAXG0060Z9N** – Slot benchmark harness: contention metrics (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+130 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+130 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+130 more)


---

## Plan (LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD, 2026-10-22)

Decomposed into three serial children (test/verification first, then the measured run, then
the verdict). Each child is a vertical slice that ends in a committed artefact (tool + tests,
committed results, updated decision doc).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Outcome |
|---|-------|------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | Quiet-window preflight gate and command validation for the slot sweep (LP-0MVK0969J004MTG3) | task | — | Fail-closed quiet gate (`/llama/local/status`) + validated command set |
| 2 | Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window (LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH) | task | 1 | Committed sweep results under `proxy/benchmarks/results/` |
| 3 | Record slot-count verdict and reconcile with projection (LP-0MVK09622002CRMR) | task | 2 | Verdict in the reevaluation doc (+ config-change item if the verdict moves) |

**Between phases:** before starting child 2, re-read child 1's recorded command set and the
queue timeout in force; before starting child 3, re-read child 2's RESULTS_NOTE validity flags
and update child 3's ACs if any run is INVALID.

### Findings that shape the plan (verified during planning)

1. **The commands in the Task section above need one correction.** `--sweep` is
   `[1, 2, 3]` (`SWEEP_SLOT_COUNTS`), so the N=1 run is included; N=1 is out of scope and was
   already measured. Use `--sweep --resume 2` for N=2/N=3, and `--slots 4` for N=4.
2. **`generate_report()` rewrites `slot_benchmark_report.json` / `_summary.txt` on every
   invocation**, so a second invocation (N=4) into the same output dir would clobber the
   N=2/N=3 report. Plan: `n2_n3/` and `n4/` subdirectories plus a preserved `report_2_3.json`.
3. **`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` is now 60 s, not 120 s** (halved by
   LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO). The parent description's 120 s assumption would make queue-timeout
   rates look incomparable with the 2026-10-17 sweep; the value in force must be recorded.
4. **The fast/cheap mode axis and the mode-switch lock are gone** (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4):
   there is a single `proxy/config.yaml` and no lock to hold — the only quiet-window risk
   left is other sessions holding local leases.
5. **Memory should not bind at N=4.** `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` shows total KV is
   constant (~2.7 GiB) and model+KV ≈ 27.4 GiB for every slot count; the real N=4 cost is the
   61,440 per-slot clamp / 58,368 warm threshold. N=4 gate: MemAvailable ≥ 40 GiB at the end
   of the N=3 run (≈27.4 GiB footprint + ~12 GiB margin).
6. **The measured N=2 baseline already exists** (production-derived, AC3 of
   LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8): prefill median 74.5 s / p90 297 s, 566 local streams,
   `finish_reason=length` 0, dispatch denied 2,635 (99.7% at `active=2`), contention queue
   799 dispatched / 4,933 abandoned (86.1%). Child 2 re-measures N=2 under controlled load so
   the three Ns are comparable; it does not replace the production baseline.
7. **The gating validity signal is local stream share.** Both prior sweeps produced
   `local share 0.0%` (everything fell back remote), so TTFT/TPS were not local numbers.
   Child 2 must report local share per N and mark a 0-share run INVALID.

### Effort/risk

Overall effort **Small**, risk **Medium** (unchanged): the work is operational, but the
outcome (verdict) is genuinely unknown and the window is externally constrained.

## Appendix: decisions taken during planning

- Q: **When is the quiet window, and who drains the herdr panes / audits?**
  Answer: not fixed by this plan and not needed to proceed — child 1 makes the precondition
  machine-checkable (fail-closed) and child 2 must stop rather than run against a busy proxy
  (matching the parent's risk note). Scheduled window remains the implementation session's
  gating step. Evidence: `curl localhost:8000/llama/local/status` shows
  `local_owner_session_id: herdr-…`, i.e. the host is *not* quiet right now.
- Q: **What MemAvailable justifies attempting N=4?**
  Answer (agent, default): ≥ 40 GiB at the end of the N=3 run. Evidence:
  `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (model+KV ≈ 27.4 GiB, total KV constant across slot
  counts), plus ~12 GiB margin. Status: defaulted; a different threshold only changes the
  skip/run decision, not the verdict rule.
- Q: **Is a new config-change item in scope here?**
  Answer: only if the verdict moves off N=2 — it is created by child 3 (AC4) and kept as a
  separate, independently schedulable item. No production config change in this item.
- Q: **Should the N=1 run be repeated for comparability?**
  Answer (agent): no. N=1 is out of scope (the decision is between 2/3/4) and its
  2026-10-17 queue-timeout figures are already recorded; the plan records that the new run
  starts at N=2 instead.
- Q: **Plan approval required?**
  Answer: no — the approval gate (`plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate`) returns
  `request_approval: false` because the item is Small effort / Medium risk, not Extra Large +
  High/Severe.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-22: initial decomposition into 3 children (preflight gate → measured sweep →
  verdict), dependencies wired (2←1, 3←2); corrected `--sweep`→`--sweep --resume 2`; recorded
  the 60 s queue timeout, the removed mode-switch lock, and the `generate_report()` overwrite
  hazard.
data.title: Run controlled N=3/N=4 slot-count sweep in a quiet window

## Goal

Regenerate the four 24 h analysis windows with the existing `analyze_proxy_usage.py` CLI and archive the raw rotated log segments covering them, **before** retention rotates them away — so every number quoted in the investigation (AC1/AC2/AC6) stays reproducible after rotation.

This runs first, in parallel with the tooling children, because log retention is not contractual (parent constraint) and the base window's rotated segments are already ~4 days old.

## Scope

No skill-code changes: uses the CLI as-is. Archiving is copy-only; log data is never edited in place.

## Work

1. Confirm each window is still resolvable from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (log clock = local Europe/Dublin):

   | name | start | end |
   |---|---|---|
   | `base24` | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 | 2026-10-19 14:37:48 |
   | `ref24` | 2026-10-19 14:44:27 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 |
   | `post24` | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 |
   | `now24` | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | 2026-10-22 14:44:27 |

2. Run the CLI once per window:

   ```
   python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "<start>" --end "<end>" \
     --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/<name>"
   ```

3. Archive raw segments covering 2026-10-18 00:00 → 2026-10-22 23:59 (`proxy.log-2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log.2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log-2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log.2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log`, plus the matching `llama-server.log*`) into `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/`, preserving the originals and verifying each copy with `gzip -t` (or `cmp`) after copy. Total is ~26 MB, so a full copy is cheap.

4. Write `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` recording, per window: the start/end boundary, the exact CLI command used, the output dir, and the headline numbers printed by the CLI (sessions, requests, logged tokens) so the parent's recorded figures can be checked against a committed command (AC6).

5. Post a comment on the parent with the archive path, the manifest path, and the four headline rows.

## Expected outcome

Four regenerated window directories plus a raw archive and manifest, so later children (and any future re-measurement) do not depend on log retention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `~/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{base24,ref24,post24,now24}/` each contain `report.md`, `standard_sessions.csv`, `low_priority_sessions.csv`, and `errors.csv`/`errors.json`.
2. Every archived segment in `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/` passes an integrity check after copy (`gzip -t`/`cmp`), and the originals under `/var/log/llama-proxy` are unmodified.
3. `manifest.txt` records, per window, the start/end boundary and the exact CLI command that produced the output.
4. `base24` and `post24` reproduce the parent's headline figures (421.7 M → 828.5 M logged tokens, 12,810 → 9,137 requests) within ±5%; any larger discrepancy is recorded with the CLI values that differ rather than silently accepted.
5. A parent comment links the archive and manifest paths, and every command used appears in the manifest.
6. No log file is edited or rewritten in place.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — used as-is for window regeneration
- `${HOME}/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` — window boundaries + reproducible commands

## Notes

- `now24` is a fourth reference window (operator decision, plan Q1A) so a single before/after pair containing seven co-landed commits is not the only evidence.
- If a window has already rotated away, record that limitation in the parent comment and use the recorded figures from the parent description as the baseline (stated fallback per the parent's assumption).
data.title: Archive and regenerate four evidence windows

# Detach-by-default launch in start-proxy.sh

Core implementation for LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY, per its "Desired change" items 1-3:
flag parsing (`--foreground`, `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1`, `--log-file`), a
detach helper around the final `exec`, the handoff line, and `--foreground`
updates to the existing shell harnesses so AC6 holds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--foreground` (or `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` for unattended callers) keeps
  today's blocking `exec` behaviour for interactive debugging. The flag is parsed
  and consumed by the script (never forwarded to uvicorn) and is documented in
  the usage header. Without it, foreground execution is not possible.
- [ ] **AC1 — Server survives the launcher's process-group death.** By default
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` performs all of its synchronous validation (port free, provider API
  keys resolved, config readable, restart/cleanup phases) and then launches uvicorn in its **own**
  session/process group (`setsid`, with a `nohup … &` + `disown` fallback when `setsid` is
  unavailable), redirecting the child's stdout/stderr to a log file (`--log-file <path>`, default
  `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`) so the caller's pipe is **not** held open. It prints a single handoff
  line (child PID, log path, health-check command) and exits 0.
- [ ] The detached re-exec passes `--foreground` and drops `--restart`, so the
  child cannot re-enter the detach path or repeat the restart storm; the uvicorn
  command line, config resolution, API-key fail-closed behaviour, restart gate
  and `--keep-llama-server` semantics are unchanged (launch-harness change only).
- [ ] Existing callers and harnesses are unaffected: the already-detached call
  patterns (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &`
  in the skill and `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh`, and `--restart`'s
  `pkill`/port-release logic) keep working, and the existing shell harnesses
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`,
  `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh`,
  `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh`) are updated with
  `--foreground` where they intentionally intercept the final `exec`, each with
  an explanatory comment, or otherwise still pass.
- [ ] `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` (and its pytest wrapper) passes, and
  `bash -n proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` is clean.

## Key Files

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — flag parser, detach helper, handoff line, usage header.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` — `--foreground` updates.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — `--foreground` updates.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh` — `--foreground` updates.
- `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh` — `--foreground` updates.

## Notes

- Depends on the RED detach test (test-first): the script change makes it green.
- Overlapping touch points with LP-0MVJX7NGN006S74K (same script, unrelated
  area) — keep edits scoped; implement sequentially.
data.title: Detach-by-default launch in start-proxy.sh
